answers.answer: In 3 players, the two tied leaders gain nothing; the unique last player pays 1 coin. In an unequal 2-player Census, the unique leader gains 1 coin and the unique last player pays nothing.
answers.evidence: Census: unique leader gains; tied lead gives no coin; tied last pays nothing; in a 2-player game the last player never pays.

answers.answer: No. Draw up to the allowance, limited by free Market spaces, so you may draw at most two and need not draw six. Unused Market Followers remain there between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Followers: draw any number up to allowance, limited by free Market spaces; unused Market Followers remain and occupy capacity.

answers.answer: You may fill an action gradually over multiple rounds, but it activates only when all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology (Town Hall needs one of two). You cannot execute it before it is full; a fully activated action may be saved for a later round. When an ordinary action is executed, its Followers return to your bag; Technology stays on its spaces.
answers.evidence: Planning; Actions: actions activate when all required spaces are occupied; activation can be saved; after an ordinary action, return Followers to bag and Technology stays.

answers.answer: Starting with Start Player and going clockwise repeatedly, each player takes one activated action or passes per turn. Passing ends your participation in Phase 5, so you cannot act again that round; unused activations keep their Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: Actions: one activated action or passing per turn, clockwise; passing ends participation; unused activations keep their Followers for future rounds.

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances your Farmers Track one space, and gives you the good depicted at that space.
answers.evidence: Actions table: Farm House—put a new Farmer in your bag; advance Farmers Track one space and take its depicted good.

answers.answer: Village can recruit a Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader, putting the chosen neutral Follower in your bag and advancing that profession's track one space. Boatman gives depicted coins (or a Citizen to the first player at the last space); Craftsman gives a Technology tile, usable only after you pass; Trader gives a Place Tile, with first advance limited to category I and later advances allowing I or II.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment: separate Boatman, Craftsman and Trader track rewards and bag placement.

answers.answer: The newly recruited Craftsman's Technology cannot help execute another action this round after you pass; it is used only after passing. Your first Technology must replace a Farmer. Technology is immovable once placed; later tiles may replace any profession except Monk; never place more than one at a Place or one at a Place requiring only one Follower. A tile acquired from Craftsman is used only after passing.
answers.evidence: Technology placement limits; Village recruitment: Craftsman tile is used only after passing.

answers.answer: No. The first Trader-track advance permits category I only; each later advance permits category I or II. Players may inspect the Place Tile stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment: first Traders Track advance permits category I only; every later advance allows I or II. Setup: players may inspect stacks at any time.

answers.answer: University recruits a Scholar into your bag, advances the Scholars Track, and gains the depicted Development Points. Castle recruits a Knight into your bag and advances Knights Track; the fourth Knight leaves draw allowance at 7 and the first player there takes its Citizen. Monastery recruits a Monk into your bag with no extra track reward. Once a character track reaches its last space, that action cannot be taken again.
answers.evidence: Actions table; Castle rewards; Character-track limits.

answers.answer: Yes, a Monk may replace a Knight (or any other profession) on an ordinary action. No, a Knight or Technology cannot replace a required Monk. No, a Monk cannot replace the exact profession required for a Beneficial Deed.
answers.evidence: Monks: may replace any other profession on ordinary actions; reverse forbidden. Deeds require exact professions; substitutions cannot replace them.

answers.answer: Ship moves your Merchant one connection along a Waterway (blue) to one adjacent town; Wagon uses one Road (brown) to one adjacent town. You may take at most one good, choosing one if two are there; taking it is optional. Empty connections are legal and yield no good.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: one adjacent town along one connection; Ship Waterway, Wagon Road; one optional good; empty connections legal.

answers.answer: Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the town where your Merchant currently is. A town with any player's station cannot receive another, except Orléans, where each player may build one station.
answers.evidence: Building: Guildhall requires Merchant in town; no station where any player's station is already built; Orléans exception.

answers.answer: Scriptorium gains 1 Development Point by moving one space on the Development Track. Moving onto or past a coin space collects its depicted coins; the first player onto or past a Citizen space collects that Citizen; reaching or passing a Development Status space immediately changes Status to its shown value.
answers.evidence: Actions table: Scriptorium. Scoring: Development Points and track spaces.

answers.answer: Town Hall can activate with either one or two neutral Followers of any profession; one action can send one or both. Your four marked starting Followers cannot be used. Permanently send each chosen Follower to a free Beneficial Deed space matching its exact profession, and take that placement's reward: depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins, or for Canalization choose 1 coin or 1 Development Point. Whoever fills a Deed's last space takes its Citizen.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: one or two; exact profession spaces; rewards including Canalization; last-space Citizen; starting Followers barred.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage forbids Monk recruitment and applies in Phase 5 (Actions), though it is revealed in Phase 1. Other normal events resolve in Phase 6. Round 1 opens with Pilgrimage because that tile is placed on top of the prepared stack.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure phases 1, 5, 6; setup Hour Glass stack.

answers.answer: Wine is food; wool is not. Paid food goes to the Goods Market. If you have no food, you owe 5 coins; with fewer than five coins, pay what you can and undergo torture for the shortfall.
answers.evidence: Harvest: pay grain, cheese, or wine to Goods Market; if unable pay food, pay 5 coins; if unable, torture for shortfall. Wool and brocade are not food. Torture payment.

answers.answer: The neutral Scholar is returned to its game-board supply and becomes recruitable again; its track marker does not move back. Your marked starting Trader is kept, you lose no Follower for that Plague, and you do not redraw.
answers.evidence: Plague: neutral Follower returns to supply, don't move track marker back; marked starting Follower is kept and do not redraw.

answers.answer: Pay the one coin you have; replace each of the two missing coins with one item for each shortfall coin. Options are a built or unbuilt Trading Station, one random eligible Follower from your bag only, one Development Point, one Goods Tile, one Place Tile, or one Technology tile. Market and Action Space Followers are ineligible; marked starting Followers must be returned and redrawn until an eligible neutral Follower is drawn. Losing a Development Point moves one space left but never onto or past a coin space. Surrendered items are removed from the game; only lost Development Points can be regained.
answers.evidence: Torture (bankruptcy): payment shortfall options and restrictions, Development Point limit, items removed, only DP regainable.

answers.answer: You cannot play an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods tile, even if another part would still reward you. It becomes available again when the required tile is available, subject to normal requirements. If the common coin supply lacks enough coins, players cannot receive coins at that moment.
answers.evidence: Limited supplies: actions requiring unavailable tiles cannot be played; become available when supply returns; insufficient coin supply prevents receipt.

answers.answer: A tie for most built Trading Stations gives the bonus Citizen to nobody. Goods score grain 1, cheese 2, wine 3, wool 4, brocade 5 points each. Built Trading Stations plus collected Citizens score (stations + Citizens) × final Development Status. Equal scores go to the player furthest ahead on Development Track; if still tied, victory is shared.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory: unique most gets set-aside Citizen; tie gets nobody; goods and station/Citizen formula; tie-break.

answers.answer: Each player receives a board, bag, Merchant, 10 Trading Stations, 5 coins, 7 markers, and four marked starting Followers. Put starting Followers on your Market, Merchant in Orléans, and one marker on the first space of each of six Character Tracks and the Development Track. Keep coins and unbuilt stations in front of you. The youngest player takes Start Player token.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2 and youngest player.

answers.answer: Place 13 Citizens on their marked board/Deed spaces and set the remaining Citizen aside for the final Trading Station award. Sort neutral Followers by profession into their game-board buildings and Technology into its supply. Separate Place Tiles into categories I and II. In 4-player games, shuffle map goods face down and deal one face up onto every eligible Road/Waterway goods space; sort remaining goods face up into the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1, 3, 5.

answers.answer: For 3 players, remove 2 neutral Farmers, Boatmen, Craftsmen and Traders each; 3 neutral Knights, Scholars and Monks each; 6 random goods; leave spaces marked 4 empty. For 2 players, remove 4 of each of the first four professions; 6 of each of the latter three; 12 random goods; leave spaces marked 3 or 4 empty. Remove all starting Followers of unused colors.
answers.evidence: Fewer players table and setup: remove starting Followers of unused colors.

answers.answer: Farm House: Boatman + Craftsman. Village: Farmer + Boatman + Craftsman. University: Farmer + Craftsman + Trader. Castle: Farmer + Boatman + Trader. Monastery: Scholar + Trader.
answers.evidence: Actions table: required professions.

answers.answer: Ship: Farmer + Boatman + Knight. Wagon: Farmer + Trader + Knight. Guildhall: Farmer + Craftsman + Knight.
answers.evidence: Actions table: required professions.

answers.answer: Scriptorium requires Knight + Scholar. Town Hall accepts any one or two neutral Followers of any profession.
answers.evidence: Actions table: required professions; Town Hall rules.

answers.answer: Yes. You may decline two draws and instead move one Follower from an Action Space back to your Market for each declined draw. You cannot move a Follower directly from one Action Space to another.
answers.evidence: Followers phase: for each draw declined, may move one from Action Space to Market; this is permitted recovery; direct action-space transfer prohibited.

answers.answer: Yes. You may inspect your bag at any time, but must shuffle its contents afterward.
answers.evidence: Followers phase: inspect bag at any time, but shuffle contents afterward.

answers.answer: The phases are Hour Glass (reveal), Census, Followers, Planning, Actions, Event, Start Player. Pass the Start Player token to the player on your left. Planning begins simultaneously; if order matters, proceed clockwise from Start Player. In Phase 6, payments and necessary order-sensitive resolution proceed clockwise from Start Player. Paid coins go to common supply; received coins come from it.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure phases 1–7; Planning and Event order; coin supply.

answers.answer: Do not score immediately. Finish the entire round in which the 18th Hour Glass tile is drawn, including its event; scoring follows.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory: finish entire round in which 18th tile is drawn, including its event; before scoring.

answers.answer: The uniquely ahead player on the Farmers Track gains 1 coin, regardless of how many Farmer tiles are in bags.
answers.evidence: Census: compare Farmers Track markers regardless of Farmer tiles currently in bags; unique leader gains 1 coin.

answers.answer: Income pays coins equal to current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Events: Income—gain coins equal to Development Status.

answers.answer: Eight goods means two complete groups of three, so pay 2 coins. Goods type does not matter; Taxes counts all goods. A shortfall causes torture.
answers.evidence: Events: Taxes counts all goods and charges 1 coin per complete group of 3, round down; shortfall causes torture.

answers.answer: You receive 4 coins, one per built Trading Station. Unbuilt reserve stations do not count.
answers.evidence: Events: Trading Day gives 1 coin per built Trading Station; scoring/building distinguishes built stations.

answers.answer: Hayrick: Farmer; 1 grain from Goods Market. Cheese Factory: Farmer + Farmer; 1 cheese from Goods Market. Winery: Farmer + Trader; 1 wine from Goods Market. Wool Manufacturer: Boatman + Trader; 1 wool from Goods Market. Tailor Shop: Scholar + Trader; 1 brocade from Goods Market. A goods-producing Place cannot be used when its particular good is absent from Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Place Tiles table and statement following it.

answers.answer: Shipping Line: Boatman; gain 1 Development Point. Brewery: Monk; gain 2 coins. Windmill: Craftsman + Craftsman; gain 2 coins and 1 Development Point. Library: Knight + Scholar; gain 2 Development Points.
answers.evidence: Place Tiles table.

answers.answer: Any one Follower activates Pharmacy. Pay 1–3 coins and advance one Development space per coin; paying two advances two spaces. Zero or four coins is not allowed.
answers.evidence: Place Tiles table: Pharmacy.

answers.answer: Cellar: Monk + Scholar; gain 4 coins. Office: Scholar + Scholar; gain 1 coin per built Trading Station. Hospital: Boatman + Scholar; gain coins equal to current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Place Tiles table.

answers.answer: Horse Wagon requires Trader + Knight. It moves along one Road to an adjacent town and collects one good if available.
answers.evidence: Place Tiles table.

answers.answer: Laboratory requires Scholar + Craftsman and gives a Technology tile, subject to usual Technology placement constraints. Your first Technology cannot be placed on Laboratory because it must replace a Farmer and Laboratory has Scholar and Craftsman spaces. A later Technology may occupy either Laboratory space if none is already there and usual constraints are met.
answers.evidence: Place Tiles table: Laboratory.

answers.answer: Bathhouse requires a Farmer. Draw three Followers from your bag, choose two, and immediately place them on appropriate Action Spaces; none may go on Bathhouse. Return the third drawn Follower and the activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: Place Tiles table: Bathhouse.

answers.answer: You may place the one Follower that can legally go onto an appropriate Action Space. Return the other two drawn Followers and the activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag. If none can be placed, place none and return all three drawn Followers and the activating Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: Bathhouse: if only one or none can legally be placed, do so and return all other drawn Followers and activating Follower to bag.

answers.answer: It may be executed on a later action turn in the same Action Phase, provided you have not passed. A Place completed during Phase 5 is available on a later one of your action turns in that phase.
answers.evidence: Actions: Place completed during Action Phase available on later one of your action turns in same phase; passing final.

answers.answer: Sacristy requires a Monk. If activated, during Phase 6 return its Monk to your bag instead of suffering a negative event such as Harvest, Taxes, or Plague.
answers.evidence: Place Tiles: Sacristy.

answers.answer: No. Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5, when actions occur. Sacristy's protection applies during Phase 6; it does not override the Phase 5 recruitment prohibition.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Pilgrimage applied Phase 5; Sacristy protects during Phase 6.

answers.answer: Herb Garden lets Boatmen replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions; it does not allow replacing Knights, Scholars, or Monks.
answers.evidence: Place Tiles table: Herb Garden lists allowed substitutions.

answers.answer: School lets Scholars replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions. It has no activation cost; it is a passive ability. A Scholar cannot replace a required Monk.
answers.evidence: Place Tiles table: School no activation; Scholars replace other professions except Monks.

answers.answer: No. Beneficial Deeds require exact professions, so substitutions cannot fill a differently depicted space. Gunpowder Tower also requires exact Deed types; using it instead of Town Hall does not change that.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: substitutions cannot replace exact professions. Gunpowder Tower: Deed spaces still require exact types.

answers.answer: Gunpowder Tower adds 2 Market spaces. During Phase 3 place 1 or 2 drawn Followers there. In Planning move one or both to Action Spaces, or in Actions send one or both directly to Beneficial Deeds in a single action. Marked starting Followers cannot be sent; Deed spaces require exact types.
answers.evidence: Place Tiles table: Gunpowder Tower.

answers.answer: The unique leader gains 1 coin. The two players tied furthest behind pay nothing because tied last place pays nothing.
answers.evidence: Census: unique leader gains; tied last place pays nothing.

answers.answer: At the end of the game, before scoring, the player with the unique most built Trading Stations receives the set-aside Citizen. That Citizen counts among collected Citizens in the station/Citizen scoring formula.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory: before scoring, unique most built stations takes set-aside Citizen; formula counts collected Citizens.

answers.answer: Remove the lighter Pilgrimage tile, shuffle the other 17 Hour Glass tiles face down, then put the removed Pilgrimage on top, so round 1 is Pilgrimage. In Phase 1 the Start Player reveals the top tile.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4; Turn Structure Phase 1.

answers.answer: Each remaining coin scores 1 victory point.
answers.evidence: Scoring table: Coins—1 each.

answers.answer: Development Status starts at 1 and initial draw allowance is 4.
answers.evidence: Setup step 2.

answers.answer: Only lost Development Points can be regained. Surrendered goods, Followers, Trading Stations, Places, and Technology are removed from the game, not returned to supplies.
answers.evidence: Torture: items removed from game; only lost Development Points can be regained.

answers.answer: You may choose the order of your actions freely.
answers.evidence: Actions: choose your actions' order freely.

answers.answer: The passive substitution ability is available immediately, including during the current Action Phase, when the Place is acquired.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment: acquired Place and passive special ability available immediately, including current Action Phase.

answers.answer: You may send just one, or both, in a Town Hall action.
answers.evidence: Town Hall: send one or both to free matching Deed spaces.

answers.answer: Taking a good is optional; you may complete the move and leave the available good on the connection.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: taking a good during Ship or Wagon movement is optional.

answers.answer: Yes. You may send the second Follower on a later action turn in the same Action Phase, before passing; the two need not be transferred in one action.
answers.evidence: FAQ: Town Hall's two Followers may be sent in separate action turns during same Action Phase, before passing.
